title: Transition in epileptology - patient knowledge and needs
summary: Approximately half of all children with epilepsy continue to be affected by epilepsy in adulthood. The transition from pediatric neurological (neuropediatric) care to adult neurology is called transition. In Germany, the transition process is often unstructured, which can lead to a loss of information and impair compliance with treatment plans and quality of life. The aim of the study is to assess the effectiveness of the Frankfurt transition concept in terms of patient satisfaction and well-being, independence, and the level of knowledge, concerns, and needs of adolescents and young adults with epilepsy and their parents during the transition from pediatric to adult care. Data is collected using questionnaires for adolescent patients with epilepsy (aged 14-21) and their parents about concerns, knowledge, and quality of life during the transition process from pediatric neurological care to adult epileptological care.

interventions.name: Adolescents with epilepsy who are treated at the Epilepsy Center Frankfurt (neuropediatrics and neurology) or at the MZEB Hattersheim are surveyed in this study using questionnaires on their knowledge of the disease and their readiness for transition, as well as the concerns and expectations of both

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Epilepsy as defined by the ILAE (International League Against Epilepsy) with age at initial diagnosis of epilepsy < 18 years and with more than one previous contact with a neuropediatrician, neuropediatric specialist consultation, or connection to a SPZ
Understanding and consent to the information provided or information provided to the legal guardian
Exclusion criteria:
No confirmed diagnosis of epilepsy
Age <14 and >= 22 years
